name: La Kir
warning: SECTOR CLOSED from 15 February to 15 June — prefectoral biotope-protection order, because peregrine falcons nest here.
notes: The routes on this sector are of exceptional quality.
routes: Sustained and consistent. Small roof with hidden holds. Athletic climbing that needs a bit of flexibility. One move where you'll have to commit.
Bouldery. One move where you'll need to have the sequence dialled. Demanding to read. Fairly pumpy overall.
Sustained. A very good stamina test at the grade. Demanding, technical climbing. A must-do.
Sustained climbing. Very intense bouldery section, slightly reach-dependent.
Physical, complex climbing. Very beautiful. Needs a good climbing rhythm and plenty of power.
Start on the right and finish on the right. Follows the line of weakness; nice route with an original line.
Same start as 'Deuxième inconnue' but finish straight up. Nice technical slab at the top. Keep something in reserve for the finish.
Slightly disconcerting direct start. Finish in the crack of 'Deuxième inconnue'.
Consistent. Beautiful technical route on a gassy (exposed) pillar. Relaxing at the rests is the key to the redpoint. Atmospheric finish. Very classy — a must-do.
Le fil à couper le beurre
Very sculpted rock. A route with character that demands commitment and determination.
Starting variant of 'Le fil à couper le beurre'. Start up route 107, then traverse left.
Fairly consistent. Beautiful moves; technical, slightly run-out climbing on the overhanging slab at the top.
Demanding climbing at the start, easier finish in the crack.
Mixed climbing, with a start that needs good route-reading. Middle section shared with 111. Finish by traversing right onto a slab. Original line.
Consistent and very varied. Keep something in reserve for the finish. A beautiful route at the grade (careful not to bully the wedged block at the top).
Not consistent; the scoop at the top is very sculpted. Belay attentively.
Finish straight up via a sculpted crack. Committing finish.
Nice route but broken up by ledges. Possible anchor halfway. There is a bees' nest on the 2nd pitch: be careful.
Hard start on a pillar; joins the anchor of 114, or can also finish up 113-1 for more consistency.
Technical, Cormot-style slab that takes a bit of intuition…
Historic route, varied styles. The summit chimney is surprising.
Physical and consistent. Bridging/opposition in a flake. Mantels and corners that aren't easy to negotiate.
Finishing variant of 118. Sustained climbing on spaced flat edges at the top of the route.
Starts left of La JP. Awkward mantel onto the ledge.
Finishing variant of 120. Follow the line of the pillar, with a mantel that needs flexibility.
Le Rambo des bacs à sable
Pillar with varied climbing and holds. Nice crimpy slab at the top.
Varied, unusual climbing. Surprising tufa column low down; the rest is really physical. Very nice route.
Complex to read. Technical route overall that needs good anticipation.
Bouldery route with a serious slab problem. Feet often on nothing much, but the route is no less interesting for it.
Slab lovers will enjoy it. Bouldery route with big moves on sloping holds.
Inconsistent and very intense on the hard moves. A 'key' move on a concave slab on micro-holds.
Curious slab start, then traverse right to reach a wide crack. Interesting climbing.
Same start as 128, then finish in the small vertical crack. Finger climbing.
Sustained climbing on flat crimps, sometimes a little spaced.
Layback (Dülfer) climbing, a little physical on the hard move, where the polish starts to show. Rising traverse left to reach the big crack.
Not consistent, with many rests on the route. Bridging and crack climbing to the fore. A section of loose rock in the second half of the route.
Les jeux des nuages et de la pluie
The Games of Clouds and Rain
Selective start, then a vertical crack and big flakes. Varied climbing.
Direct start to route 132. Lacks consistency.
The Year of the Grand Pianos
Intense moves broken up by good rests; keep a bit in reserve for the finish.
Sustained and consistent. Overhanging slab on small holds and a pillar climbed with finesse.
